newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania unveils new 1997 privatisation list.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania unveils new 1997 privatisation list.

text.p: Lithuania's state privatisation agency on Wednesday unveiled a new list of companies for sale in 1997 but key companies such as the state airline and telecommunications firm were not on the list.
"The list has 778 companies with a nominal value of 778 million litas," Lithuanian Privatisation Agency head Vytas Atkochiunas told a news conference.
Lithuania's new right-of-centre government has sell-off said it wants to speed up privatisation and in its government programme named Lithuanian Telecom as one of the firms it wants to sell.
The list includes firms in several sectors, including one of the main hotels in Vilnius.
The current 1997 list was drawn up under the former government and Aktochiunas said the agency hoped to put the telecoms firm on the list later.
"We initially included Lithuanian Airlines but the transport ministry removed it," he said. "We hope the new government will allow us to put it back on."
Lithuania carried out a successful first wave of privatisation by selling most residential dwellings and smaller companies but the large state-owned firms remained firmly in government hands.
The slow pace of this part of the privatisation process has been blamed for the low level of foreign investment in Lithuania compared to its neighbours Latvia and Estonia.
"The new government has promised to privatise most things that have not been sold to date," privatisation commission chairman Eduardas Vilkis said.
"To promote privatisation we must either lower the prices asked or simplify the procedures," he added.
German bank Deutsche Bank said in recent reports that $359 million in foreign capital was invested in Lithuania by end-1995 versus $701 million in Estonia by the start of March 1996.
